steps.label: Addition Rules
steps.content:
Addition Rules

  • Binary addition works column by column, right to left, just like denary addition.
  • Add the two bits in a column, plus any carry that arrived from the column to the right.
  • A total of 2 means write 0 and carry 1 to the next column.
  • A total of 3 means write 1 and carry 1 to the next column.
Column totalWriteCarry
0 + 000
0 + 110
1 + 101
1 + 1 + 111

steps.label: Check Your Understanding
steps.content:
Check Your Understanding

Questions to ask around the room:

  • What do you write when a column total is 2?
  • What do you write when a column total is 3?
  • Which direction do you work when adding binary columns?
  • What do you do with a carry that comes out of a column?

steps.label: Carry Chains
steps.content:
Carry Chains

  • A carry chain happens when a carry lands on a column that is also a 1, producing another carry.
  • The chain keeps moving left as long as it keeps landing on 1s.
  • The chain stops the first time it lands on a column where both bits are 0, that column becomes a 1 with nothing left to carry.
  • Adding just 1 to a run of 1s, like 00001111, always produces a carry chain.
